title: Adverse event following immunization or vaccination in children in Minas Gerais: 2015 to 2020.
ehr_evidence: Data for this study were collected in January 2022, using ESAVI notifications resulting from immunization errors registered in SI-PNI.
summary: Ecological descriptive study analyzing immunization errors and adverse events following immunization in children aged 0-9 years in Minas Gerais, Brazil, from 2015 to 2020 using national immunization registry data.
key_findings: 3,259 immunization error events were recorded out of 39,903,277 doses administered (0.008%).
91.86% of immunization errors did not result in adverse events.
56.02% of errors occurred in children under 1 year of age.
The most frequent error diagnosis was application outside the recommended age (29.12%).
Fever was the most common manifestation (40.85%), with 71.91% of events being local or systemic.
Incidence rates were 7.50/100,000 doses for errors without adverse events and 0.66/100,000 for errors with adverse events.
2019 recorded the highest incidence rates for both error categories.
population: children aged 0-9 years in Minas Gerais, Brazil
limitations: underreporting of adverse events following immunization
lack of simultaneous implementation of the notification system across all macro-regions
potential underreporting due to fear of professional reprimand
